input: wordlist and queries are lists of 0 through 5000 strings each; every string contains 1 through 7 ASCII English letters A-Z or a-z. Empty outer lists are explicit extensions. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: One result string for each query, preserving query order. Prefer an exact case-sensitive word; otherwise the earliest wordlist entry matching case-insensitively; otherwise the earliest entry matching after case-folding and treating each vowel a/e/i/o/u as interchangeable at the same position. Return an empty string if no rule matches.
mutation_aliasing: Both caller lists and all their string values are unchanged. A fresh result container may contain immutable original query/wordlist strings or the empty string. Private exact, case-normalized and vowel-normalized lookup structures retain only the first normalized match. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: ASCII-only lowercasing cannot change length or require locale-sensitive rules. Every counter/index is bounded by 5000 or 7; results are strings, not numeric coercions. The * mask is outside the accepted alphabet, making fixed-position vowel normalization unambiguous.
complexity: Let S be total input characters and Q the number of queries. O(S+Q+1) expected time includes lowercasing, masked-key construction and string hashing/comparison; vowel membership tests inspect at most five characters. O(S_wordlist+Q+1) retained lookup/output space plus O(7) transient key buffers. Query normalization allocates O(S_queries) total characters, not all retained simultaneously. Map/set costs assume ordinary average O(1) operations after charging key construction/hash/comparison; no universal ECMAScript constant-time or adversarial collision-resistance guarantee is claimed.
